title: Ancient DNA Extraction Part I: Lysate Preparation
author: Sarah Nagel
materials: Thoroughly vortex the lysate tubes after thawing.
Start the FluidX barcode reader software and allow the camera to initialize.

If stored at −20 °C, remove the lysates from the freezer and thaw at room temperature for at least 30 minutes. Alternatively, thaw the lysates in a Thermo shaker at 37 °C for approximately 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the Proteinase K solution and the extraction‑buffer stock solution exactly as described in the MATERIALS section.

steps.title: Decontaminate LoBind tubes
steps.instruction: Decontaminate all 2.0 ml LoBind tubes according to the procedure given in the MATERIALS section.

steps.title: Calculate volumes and create IDs
steps.instruction:
Open the ‘Subsamples’ tab of the “samples_to_screen” list (P:\AncientDNA\samples). Identify the subsamples to be lysed, count the number of controls, and calculate the required volumes of extraction‑buffer stock solution and Proteinase K solution for each subsample weight class, always adding an excess equivalent to one additional reaction. Use the table below:

Subsample (mg) | Extraction buffer (µl) | Buffer stock (µl) | Proteinase K (µl)
<10 | 300 | 292.5 | 7.5
11‑25 | 500 | 487.5 | 12.5
26‑99 | 1000 | 975 | 25
100‑200 | 2000 | 1950 | 50

Add an extraction negative control (ENC) for every set of 20 subsamples by adding the corresponding amount of extraction buffer to an empty tube and labeling it ‘ENC’. Create lysate IDs in CoreDB, move the subsamples from the ‘Subsamples’ tab to the ‘Lysates’ tab, fill all required fields, save a copy of the updated list with date and initials, and place the previous version in the “screening_list_backup” folder.

steps.title: Create Labfolder entry
steps.instruction: Before starting the bench work, create a new experiment entry in Labfolder. Name the entry with the Labfolder template name followed by the lysate IDs. Fill all provided data‑element fields; these will later be used to generate the CoreDB entry. Ensure lysate IDs have been created before proceeding.

steps.title: Spin and label subsample tubes
steps.instruction: Spin the subsample tubes in a mini‑centrifuge to collect the material at the bottom. Label each tube with its lysate ID, the current date, and your initials (place the new label on top of the old subsample label).

steps.title: Make extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Combine the calculated volumes of extraction‑buffer stock solution and Proteinase K solution in a 50 ml Falcon tube (or in a 250 ml bottle for large volumes). Mix by shaking to obtain a ready‑to‑use extraction buffer containing 0.25 mg ml⁻¹ Proteinase K. If prepared in a 250 ml bottle, transfer the mixture to a 50 ml Falcon tube for easier pipetting.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer to subsamples
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate amount of the prepared extraction buffer to each subsample tube as calculated (open only one tube at a time). Record the reagent information in the corresponding fields of the Labfolder entry.

steps.title: Thaw Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Thaw the Proteinase K stock at room temperature, vortex briefly, and spin down before use.

steps.title: Incubate tubes overnight
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a rotating incubator set to 37 °C and rotate them overnight (minimum 8 h). Record the incubation start time in Labfolder.

steps.title: Post‑incubation handling
steps.instruction: After the overnight incubation, briefly spin the tubes, then either store them in the freezer until further processing or proceed directly to lysate aliquoting (Option A = FluidX, Option B = manual). Record the incubation end time in Labfolder and update the storage location in CoreDB.

steps.title: Spin lysate tubes
steps.instruction: Spin all lysate tubes at maximum speed for 5 minutes in a tabletop centrifuge inside the sample hood. Handle the tubes gently to avoid disturbing the fragile pellet.

steps.title: Prepare FluidX rack
steps.instruction: Insert empty FluidX tubes column‑wise into one or more FluidX racks, using only odd‑numbered columns (1, 3, 5, …) and leaving even columns empty. After each ENC, start a new column. Label each rack with the lysate IDs, date, and initials.

steps.title: Scan FluidX barcodes
steps.instruction: Use the FluidX barcode reader to scan the barcode on the bottom of every empty tube in the rack and to read the rack ID displayed on the front.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to FluidX
steps.instruction: Transfer 150 µl of supernatant from each lysate tube into the matching FluidX tube (verify IDs with the list created in step 3). Open only one lysate tube at a time. If the pellet begins to dissolve, repeat the centrifugation step (step 11) before transferring. If a lysate contains less than 150 µl, transfer the entire remaining volume and top up to 150 µl with extraction‑buffer stock solution. Update the lysate‑input column in the “samples_to_screen” list and mark the lysate as ‘used up’ in CoreDB. Do not remove FluidX tubes from the rack; if removal is unavoidable, re‑scan the rack and update barcodes accordingly.

steps.title: Save FluidX barcode file
steps.instruction: Move the FluidX barcode data file from "/home/public/AncientDNA/FluidX BarCodeReader/FluidX_Data/FluidX_ROOM" to your personal folder "/home/public/AncientDNA/FluidX BarCodeReader/FluidX_Data/NAME" and add the lysate IDs (step 3) to the corresponding FluidX IDs in the file.

steps.title: Close FluidX columns
steps.instruction: Close the current column of FluidX tubes with the decapper. Then open the next full or partial column (step 20) and repeat the transfer (step 14) until all lysate supernatants have been moved.

steps.title: Store FluidX rack
steps.instruction: Place the sealed FluidX rack in the freezer until further processing and return the original lysate tubes to the freezer.

steps.title: Update samples list with FluidX info
steps.instruction: Open the “samples_to_screen” list (P:\AncientDNA\samples) and add the FluidX rack ID and each FluidX tube ID to the appropriate fields. Save a copy with date and initials and move the previous version to the “screening_list_backup” folder.

steps.title: Place lysate tubes in rack
steps.instruction: Place the 2.0 ml LoBind tubes containing the lysates into a tube rack. If any lysates were frozen, thaw them at room temperature before proceeding.

steps.title: Open FluidX caps
steps.instruction: Open the first column of empty FluidX tubes using the decapper and place the caps on a clean cap rack; the caps will be needed later when closing the FluidX tubes.

steps.title: Spin lysate tubes again
steps.instruction: Spin the lysate tubes at maximum speed for 5 minutes in a tabletop centrifuge inside the sample hood, handling them gently to avoid disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to LoBind
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate supernatant (up to 150 µl or the entire remaining volume) into a new 1.5 ml or 2.0 ml LoBind tube, avoiding any sample powder. If the pellet begins to dissolve, repeat the centrifugation step (step 21) before transferring.

steps.title: Store lysate aliquot
steps.instruction: Store the tube containing the lysate aliquot in the freezer until further processing and return the remaining lysate tubes to the freezer.

steps.title: Vortex to resuspend powder
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes to fully resuspend the sample powder. Ensure the tubes are tightly closed to prevent leakage during any subsequent overnight incubation.
